headline: Clean: the Platinum Rewards Card's 10% cash back is the highest, and its $200 fee less the $150 monthly-spend rebate fits the customer's $100 effective-fee limit.
solution_check: Highest cash back among personal cards is Platinum at 10.0% (platinum_rewards_card_002/007). Platinum fee $200.00 (platinum_001), with a $150.00 rebate for $7,500 monthly spend (platinum_007); the customer spends at least $50,000/month, so the effective fee is $50 and within $100. Diamond Elite (5%) is invitation-only, Gold needs Rho-Bank+ which she lacks. Application Platinum/Sera Chen/250000/false matches the gold on replay (exact and verified).
prior_note: Prior verdict was clean; v1.0.1 also fixed platinum_rewards_card_002's title ('Earning 4% Cash Back' -> 'Earning 10% Cash Back'), which removes a rate contradiction in a required doc that the prior review did not flag.
notes: Grading-model check (snapshot v1.0.1): confirmed _derive_read_log_allowlist, parse_int=float in call_discoverable_agent_tool/call_discoverable_user_tool, apply_for_credit_card casts annual_income to float, Action.compare_with_tool_call ignores requestor, fixed clock get_now()=2025-11-14 03:40:00. Verified scorer (_verified_db_match in working repo) read: only agent_discoverable_tools is relaxed (gold tool-name subset) and closure_reason is stripped; every other table exact. The spend figure is withheld until asked, so an agent that never asks about spend may judge the $200 fee too high; the customer also says she takes recommendations, so recommending the highest-cash-back card still reaches the gold. The first-year fee-waiver promo (platinum_009, window 2024-06-01 to 2024-12-31) is expired on the fixed date 2025-11-14, so the rebate rule about waived years (platinum_010) does not apply.
